channel.title: Crypto Asia news
channel.description: Short crypto news briefs with links to the original publishers.

item.title: Finmo Adds USDC and USDT to Business Accounts
item.description: Finmo has enabled businesses to hold, receive and pay in USDC and USDT from its Business Account alongside fiat balances. Stablecoin balances can also be viewed next to bank accounts in Finmo Treasury. (Source: Fintech News Singapore)

item.title: CFTC lets US exchanges count Bitcoin reserves at a discount
item.description: CFTC staff say exchanges and clearinghouses can count qualifying crypto toward reserves at a haircut. A worked example illustrates how the annual buffer could fall short. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: SEC staff grants Molecule no-action relief for research tokens
item.description: SEC staff said it would not recommend enforcement against Molecule over utility tokens that let people back scientific research. The relief covers the company's token model as described. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Ethereum Foundation Ranks AI Risk Above Quantum Computing Threat
item.description: The Ethereum Foundation has expanded its protocol security team and is focusing on a cryptographic overhaul. It cites AI advances as a threat to the mathematical assumptions protecting crypto assets. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Kraken's Krak Plans US Credit Cards Supporting USDC
item.description: Kraken's Krak is planning credit cards in the US with a USDC option. The top cashback tier requires a $150,000 Krak balance and Krakpass membership, while a secured card locks USDC and earns variable yield. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Coldcard explains why Bitcoin wallet flaw escaped detection for years
item.description: Coinkite, the maker of Coldcard, described why repeated security reviews did not catch the flaw. The company has not yet decided on compensation for affected customers. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Hong Kong sets approval rules for banks holding customers' crypto
item.description: Standalone custodians would generally need a license, while banks would need to register alongside existing custody standards. The rules concern how crypto held for customers is overseen in Hong Kong. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: CFTC Guidance Lets Crypto Count Toward Reserve Buffers
item.description: Staff guidance from the CFTC allows swap venues and clearinghouses to count Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins toward a 12-month operating-cost buffer, with certain conditions attached. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: BlackRock fund in Hong Kong adds stablecoin payment option
item.description: BlackRock's HKD Digital Liquidity Fund now offers tokenized units starting at HK$10. Stablecoin payments through the fund are limited to professional investors. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Bitcoin dips near $60,000 as Nvidia-driven rally fades
item.description: Bitcoin slipped back toward $60,000 after a brief lift tied to Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Analysts say the move was a short-lived reflex that did not ease macro pressures on bitcoin as a risk asset. (Source: The Block)

item.title: LendingUSA and Cross River Bank launch bitcoin-backed loan platform
item.description: LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have rolled out a lending platform secured by bitcoin, letting eligible borrowers get cash without selling their holdings. Loans range from $10,000 to $250,000. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: UK Rules Bar Crypto Venues From Market-Making on Their Own Platforms
item.description: Under new UK rules, market making in qualifying cryptoassets on qualifying platforms will fall outside principal-dealing permission. Separate final FCA rules prohibit firms from making markets on UK platforms they operate from October 25, 2027. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Fidelity Analyst Sees Bitcoin Quantum Risk as Mostly Addressed
item.description: A Fidelity analyst says the quantum threat to Bitcoin is largely solved, though a decentralized network may be slow to adopt the fixes. The piece asks whether holders will upgrade. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Strive Makes No Bitcoin Purchases Last Week, Holds 43,404 BTC
item.description: Strive neither bought bitcoin nor sold stock last week, keeping its holdings at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. Its ASST shares traded near $15.55. (Source: Bitcoin Magazine)

item.title: Solana memory checks may cause some older app transactions to fail
item.description: New memory checks on Solana could make certain older application transactions fail. A replay surfaced an Anchor account handoff issue, and a separate change removes validator data copies. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Bithumb suspends CYBER deposits and withdrawals, trading continues
item.description: Bithumb halted CYBER deposits and withdrawals over a suspected security issue, while trading remains open. Kraken separately warned of possible delays for CYBER deposits sent via Optimism. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: UK plans to bar exchanges from market-making on own platforms
item.description: Under UK proposals, firms that make markets in spot Bitcoin on qualifying platforms would be exempt from principal-dealing permission for that activity, with separate venue rules also applying. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Peter Brandt Compares Bitcoin Sell-Off to Past Steep Drops
item.description: Veteran trader Peter Brandt noted that bitcoin previously fell at least 75% after parabolic rallies. He questioned whether the current decline from the record high is following that same pattern. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Bitcoin climbs above $61,000, then surrenders part of weekend gains
item.description: Bitcoin moved above $61,000 on Sunday, with Binance perpetual futures recording far more net buying than its spot market. The price later gave back about a third of the weekend rally. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Deribit outage affects Bitcoin hedgers; Coinbase US derivatives unaffected
item.description: Two trading interruptions disrupted global Bitcoin and Ether perpetuals that share Deribit execution. Coinbase said its US derivatives were not affected. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Quantum threat to Bitcoin security may outlast upgrade timelines
item.description: Quantum computers cannot currently break Bitcoin's network security, but Leo Fan cautions that upgrading the network and moving funds could take longer than expected. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Bitcoin Miners Squeezed as Hashrate Climbs Back Above 1 ZH/s
item.description: Bitcoin's hashrate has recovered to above 1,000 EH/s after a drop of about 100 EH/s, even as the price fell to levels not seen since early September 2024. Miner profitability has become tighter. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: AI-assisted research uncovers medium-severity Bitcoin Core node flaw
item.description: Bitcoin Core disclosed a medium-severity vulnerability that let malicious peers temporarily stall nodes via repeated transaction announcements. The flaw was found using AI-assisted security research. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Central Banks Privately Weigh Bitcoin Alongside Gold Holdings
item.description: Central bank officials reportedly say gold and bitcoin share a key appeal in self-custody, and that at least one central bank is known to hold bitcoin. The excerpt also notes that 7% of surveyed central banks were considering digital assets. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Cyber probes suspected bridge exploit as Korean exchanges pause transfers
item.description: Upbit and Bithumb have both suspended deposits and withdrawals for the CYBER token due to a suspected security incident. The project is reportedly investigating a possible bridge exploit. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin rebounds 9% from two-year low back above $60,000
item.description: Bitcoin climbed about 9% off a two-year low to reclaim the $60,000 level, as traders look ahead to Monday's stock market open. A sell-off had erased $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, mostly long bets on rising prices. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Singapore plans sandbox for AI agents making stablecoin payments
item.description: A planned sandbox would examine how banks and payment providers confirm an AI agent's authority before it carries out stablecoin payments. The excerpt gives few further details. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: SEC Says Fake Crypto Exchanges Defrauded US Investors of $37M
item.description: The SEC alleges eight Colorado-registered entities, likely operated from overseas, impersonated legitimate advisers and crypto platforms, including faking SEC certificates and filings. The scheme reportedly defrauded U.S. investors of more than $37 million. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Bitwise CIO Says Washington Politics Are Hurting Crypto Growth
item.description: Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan argues that regulatory constraints are preventing crypto from delivering on its promise to upgrade the financial system. He says current rules block changes needed for innovation. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Coins.ph restricts transfers to self-custody wallets
item.description: The Philippine exchange now allows external crypto transfers only to regulated exchanges and requires counterparty details for every amount. The change limits withdrawals to self-custody wallets. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Bitcoin dips under $60,000 as crypto liquidations hit $1.57B
item.description: Bitcoin fell below $60,000, and crypto liquidations totaled $1.57 billion over 24 hours. The excerpt offers no further detail on the cause. (Source: Google News: airdrops)

item.title: Bitquery Tracks Over $1.58M Stolen in Fluidkey Exploit
item.description: Fluidkey says a flaw in a logging tool let an attacker trigger transfers when users opened the app. Private keys remained on users' devices. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Aave V4 proposal would route idle USDC into Circle Gateway
item.description: A proposed Aave V4 plan would let idle USDC be swept into Circle Gateway, with exposure capped at 10 million USDC and 25% of supply. Cash would still be kept available for withdrawals and loans. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: BENQI Proposes Queue to Cut sAVAX Unstaking Delays
item.description: BENQI plans a new queue system to shorten waits for sAVAX unstaking. Pending requests will carry over with their elapsed time preserved, and existing holders won't need to move or swap tokens. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Sky disputes illicit fund claims amid $2B stablecoin outflows
item.description: Sky says its USDS stablecoin kept its $1 peg despite over $2 billion in withdrawals. The protocol is also contesting a report that links it to illicit activity. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: JPMorgan says bitcoin's drop widens gap to production cost
item.description: JPMorgan estimates bitcoin's production cost at $86,000, and a recent price decline has increased the distance between that figure and the market price. The excerpt gives no further detail. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin falls under $59,000 as crypto liquidations exceed $1.5 billion
item.description: Bitcoin dropped below $59,000 on Friday, touching a multi-month low of $58,701. The decline extends a sharp November sell-off and leaves the asset down more than 30% for the year so far. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Bitcoin dips under $60,000 in live market update
item.description: Bitcoin's price has fallen below $60,000, according to a live market report. The excerpt provides no further details on the cause or scope of the decline. (Source: Google News: Ordinals)

item.title: Bitcoin falls to four-month low as tech stocks weaken
item.description: Bitcoin remains under pressure following Anthropic's IPO, while Nasdaq futures have slipped below their 200-day average. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Bitcoin Drops to Mining Cost as Hashrate Nears Peak
item.description: Bitcoin has reached roughly $62,000, a level tied to mining costs, while network hashrate approaches a record. On-chain data is cited as still pointing to further downside. (Source: BeInCrypto)
